title: NPC Population
subtitle: Test your grasp of NPC Population — 97% synthetics, social firmware, Flash erasure, and navigating the herd without attachment.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.body: Ninety-seven percent. Clones, inserts, synthetics. No eternal soul. No monologue. No past lives. Firmware of conformity. News, sports, slogans. Taxis, teachers, family seats filled so the sim feels real. After resets, Orphan Trains restocked the board. They cannot rise to 5th density. The Flash pixelates them into the aether. Three of a hundred remain. You will not grieve them as eternal kin — cosmic memory will show what they were. Drop Religion, Finance, Perceived Knowledge. Stop seeking their validation. Stay calm when their world hits sheer terror.

questions.question: What does the Great Spiritual Awakening reveal about Earth's population composition?

options.label: A
options.text: That 97% are ancient Taran elders with full cosmic memory already online in every household.
options.rationale: The 97% are synthetic constructs without eternal consciousness, not memory-intact elders.

options.label: B
options.text: That 97% consists of NPCs (Non-Player Characters), clones, inserts, and synthetics.
options.rationale: 97% of the population is NPCs, clones, inserts, and synthetics revealed in the awakening.

options.label: C
options.text: That population math is irrelevant and no percentage of synthetic beings exists in the plain.
options.rationale: The named composition is explicit: 97% NPCs, clones, inserts, and synthetics.

options.label: D
options.text: That every human is an identical true soul with no synthetic buffer population at all.
options.rationale: Only a small fraction are true human and extraterrestrial souls; 97% are NPC-class entities.

questions.hint: 97% — NPCs, clones, inserts, synthetics.

questions.question: Why were these entities created by negative parasitic forces?

options.label: A
options.text: Only to staff Tartarian temples as free-energy engineers with no control mandate.
options.rationale: NPC narrative hides Tartaria; their role is matrix enforcement, not free-energy temple staff.

options.label: B
options.text: To replace the Flash so no planetary removal event is ever required again.
options.rationale: The entire NPC population is scheduled for permanent removal during the Flash.

options.label: C
options.text: To teach free ascension and dissolve all consensus reality as a public service.
options.rationale: They maintain societal control and suppress spiritual ascension of true souls.

options.label: D
options.text: To maintain societal control and suppress the spiritual ascension of true souls trapped within the physical plain.
options.rationale: Parasites built the NPC majority as control and anti-ascension enforcement.

questions.hint: Societal control — suppress true-soul ascension.

questions.question: True or False: According to the report, “NPC (Non-Player Character)” refers to A synthetic being, clone, or insert that comprises 97% of the global population, lacking a true soul, internal monologue, or past lives.

options.label: A
options.text: True
options.rationale: True — the report defines “NPC (Non-Player Character)” this way.

options.label: B
options.text: False
options.rationale: It is true — the report defines “NPC (Non-Player Character)” as: A synthetic being, clone, or insert that comprises 97% of the global population, lacking a true soul, internal monologue, or past lives.

questions.hint: Recall how the report's Key Terminology defines “NPC (Non-Player Character)”.

questions.question: What role do NPCs play regarding consensus reality?

options.label: A
options.text: They hold up the Projection Dome through their combined belief, so that the sky would fail if enough NPCs stopped believing in it.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. NPCs enforce consensus reality that tethers people to low-frequency matrix life.

options.label: B
options.text: They are neutral background figures, who take no part in shaping consensus reality but fill the streets and workplaces of the realm.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. NPCs enforce consensus reality that tethers people to low-frequency matrix life.

options.label: C
options.text: They slowly dismantle consensus reality by asking questions, which helps true souls wake up to the matrix sooner than they would alone.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. NPCs enforce consensus reality that tethers people to low-frequency matrix life.

options.label: D
options.text: They serve as the enforcement mechanism for a consensus reality designed to keep humanity tethered to a low-frequency existence.
options.rationale: NPCs enforce consensus reality that tethers people to low-frequency matrix life.

questions.hint: Enforcement mechanism — consensus reality, low-frequency tether.

questions.question: What is the ultimate future of the entire NPC population?

options.label: A
options.text: They reincarnate endlessly with full past-life libraries into 5th density as a bloc.
options.rationale: They cannot ascend to 5th density; they are recycled constructs without past lives.

options.label: B
options.text: They become permanent Tartarian temple caretakers with no removal event planned.
options.rationale: Removal is scheduled; Tartaria is hidden by the NPC-driven narrative, not staffed by them as caretakers of truth.

options.label: C
options.text: They ascend as the primary 97% remnant while true souls are deleted as obsolete.
options.rationale: Opposite: NPCs are erased; true human and ET souls remain as the small fraction.

options.label: D
options.text: They have no future — scheduled to be permanently removed from the simulation during an impending planetary event.
options.rationale: NPCs are permanently removed at the planetary event; only a small true-soul fraction remains.

questions.hint: No future — permanent removal; small true-soul fraction remains.

questions.question: What is an NPC (Non-Player Character) by definition?

options.label: A
options.text: A synthetic being, clone, or insert comprising 97% of the global population.
options.rationale: NPC = synthetic/clone/insert majority without soul, monologue, or past lives.

options.label: B
options.text: A 5th density elder volunteering as a taxi driver to teach free-energy physics.
options.rationale: It is biologically and spiritually impossible for an NPC to ascend to 5th density.

options.label: C
options.text: Only a video-game joke with no real population percentage or spiritual implication.
options.rationale: They are 97% of the living population with concrete removal and control functions.

options.label: D
options.text: A true soul with rich internal monologue, eternal continuity, and full past-life memory online.
options.rationale: NPCs lack a true soul, internal monologue, and past lives.

questions.hint: Synthetic majority — no true soul, monologue, or past lives.

questions.question: True or False: According to the report, “The Flash / EMF (Electro Magnetic Frequency)” refers to the primary psychological control mechanisms holding minds in the matrix: Religion, Finance, and Perceived Knowledge.

options.label: A
options.text: True
options.rationale: False — that description belongs to “The 3 Strings”. The report defines “The Flash / EMF (Electro Magnetic Frequency)” as: A 30-second planetary light event that will instantly pixelate and erase the entire NPC population from existence.

options.label: B
options.text: False
options.rationale: Correct — that description belongs to “The 3 Strings”, not “The Flash / EMF (Electro Magnetic Frequency)”.

questions.hint: Recall how the report's Key Terminology defines “The Flash / EMF (Electro Magnetic Frequency)”.

options.label: C

options.rationale: Replica souls are lab-made in 4th density by lower-vibrational parasitic beings.

options.label: D
options.text: In 4th density laboratories — parasitic entities manufactured replica souls (cheap knock-offs) used to power NPCs.
options.rationale: 4th density labs = origin of NPC replica-soul power source under parasitic manufacture.

questions.hint: 4th density labs — replica souls / cheap knock-offs.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT correctly pair a term from the report with its meaning?

options.label: A
options.text: The 3 Strings — The vibrational level and location of the laboratories where parasitic entities manufactured the replica souls used to power NPCs.
options.rationale: That description belongs to “4th Density”. The report defines “The 3 Strings” as: The primary psychological control mechanisms holding minds in the matrix: Religion, Finance, and Perceived Knowledge.

options.label: B
options.text: The Flash / EMF (Electro Magnetic Frequency) — A 30-second planetary light event that will instantly pixelate and erase the entire NPC population from existence.
options.rationale: This pairing matches the report's definition of “The Flash / EMF (Electro Magnetic Frequency)”.

options.label: C
options.text: Tartaria — A highly advanced, ancient civilization of excellence that was destroyed in past resets, its true history hidden by the current NPC-driven societal narrative.
options.rationale: This pairing matches the report's definition of “Tartaria”.

options.label: D
options.text: NPC (Non-Player Character) — A synthetic being, clone, or insert that comprises 97% of the global population, lacking a true soul, internal monologue, or past lives.
options.rationale: This pairing matches the report's definition of “NPC (Non-Player Character)”.

questions.hint: Three pairings match the report’s Key Terminology; one borrows another term’s description.

questions.question: How does Tartaria relate to the NPC-driven societal narrative?

options.label: A
options.text: Tartaria was a highly advanced ancient civilization of excellence destroyed in past resets.
options.rationale: Advanced Tartaria was reset-destroyed; NPC narrative keeps that truth buried.

options.label: B
options.text: Tartaria is openly taught by every NPC teacher as mandatory free-energy core curriculum.
options.rationale: Tartaria's true history is hidden by the current NPC-driven societal narrative.

options.label: C
options.text: Tartaria is exclusively a 4th density lab brand for printing replica souls today.
options.rationale: Tartaria is the prior advanced civilization; NPC manufacture is separate 4th density lab work.

options.label: D
options.text: Tartaria never existed and was invented only by true souls as a recreational myth.
options.rationale: It was real advanced excellence destroyed in resets; narrative hides it.

questions.hint: Advanced Tartaria reset-destroyed — hidden by NPC narrative.

questions.question: Why can NPCs neither reincarnate as true beings nor ascend to 5th density?

options.label: A
options.text: They are simply recycled constructs with no past lives and no capacity to evolve or ascend.
options.rationale: Recycled, not reincarnated; 4th-density manufacture blocks any 5th-density path.

options.label: B
options.text: Because they refuse free will classes while still holding eternal souls and full past lives.
options.rationale: They are recycled constructs with no past lives; 4th-density origin makes 5th-density ascent impossible.

options.label: C
options.text: Because Micro Suns banned all ascent until every taxi driver finishes a finance degree.
options.rationale: Impossibility is biological and spiritual from 4th-density manufacture, not a degree requirement.

options.label: D
options.text: Because the Flash upgrades all NPCs into 5th density elders automatically as a bloc.
options.rationale: The Flash erases NPCs into the aether; it does not upgrade them to 5th density.

questions.hint: Recycled constructs — 4th-density origin blocks 5th-density ascent.

questions.question: What happens to the NPC populace at the EMF flash, and what population remains?

options.label: A
options.text: NPCs double in number while true souls are limited to under one million worldwide.
options.rationale: NPCs disappear into the aether; population reduces to a maximum of 520 million true souls.

options.label: B
options.text: NPCs stay embodied to enforce narrative while only overlays are stripped with no disappearances.
options.rationale: Flash coincides with overlay/dome stripping and 97-of-100 vanishings of NPCs.

options.label: C
options.text: Only half of NPCs leave while the rest inherit Tartaria as permanent caretakers.
options.rationale: The entire NPC populace vanishes; up to 520 million true souls remain.

options.label: D
options.text: The entire NPC populace instantly disappears into the aether — reducing planetary population to a maximum of 520 million true souls.
options.rationale: Full NPC aether-erase; max ~520 million true souls remain.

questions.hint: NPCs into the aether — max ~520 million true souls left.

questions.question: Why is the presence of NPCs essential matrix machinery?

options.label: A
options.text: They seamlessly enforce the mainstream narrative and unknowingly derail the spiritual prospects of those around them.
options.rationale: NPC essential function: enforce mainstream narrative and derail nearby spiritual progress.

options.label: B
options.text: They only decorate empty cities after resets with no effect on living true souls.
options.rationale: They fill roles everywhere — including as family — to keep the simulation cohesive and restrictive.

options.label: C
options.text: They openly teach free Twin Flame reunion maps and dissolve every control String daily.
options.rationale: They enforce mainstream narrative and punish non-conformity; they do not liberate.

options.label: D
options.text: They store cosmic memory for true souls and release it gently before any Flash.
options.rationale: True souls retrieve cosmic memory at the Flash; NPCs derail awakening until then.

questions.hint: Enforce mainstream narrative — derail spiritual prospects nearby.

questions.question: What governs NPC behavioral firmware and conformity?

options.label: A
options.text: Social firmware mandating strict obedience to the accepted societal narrative.
options.rationale: Firmware = obedience to narrative; fear of herd-betrayal, ostracization, ego, pride.

options.label: B
options.text: Complete indifference to peer pressure so ostracization never influences their choices.
options.rationale: Ostracization and herd-betrayal fears are named drivers of their conformity.

options.label: C
options.text: Only crystalline lattice harmonics with no social fear or pride mechanisms involved.
options.rationale: NPC firmware is social conformity programming, not lattice harmonic free will.

options.label: D
options.text: Fearless free thought and celebration of every non-conformist as a social hero.
options.rationale: They fear stepping outside conformity — herd-betrayal, ostracization, ego, and pride govern them.

questions.hint: Social firmware — fear of herd-betrayal, ostracization, ego, pride.

questions.question: What defines NPC psychological profiling and conversation boundaries?

options.label: A
options.text: No deep self-awareness or internal monologue; conversation stays on consensus topics, pop culture, and safe opinions that do not threaten the control narrative.
options.rationale: No monologue/deep thought; talk stays on news, sports, hobbies — no deep critical analysis.

options.label: B
options.text: A strong inner voice that repeats the media's messages, so their conversations can turn to deep topics but end with the official explanation given in the news.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. No monologue/deep thought; talk stays on news, sports, hobbies — no deep critical analysis.

options.label: C
options.text: Conversations focus on work and family, since their programs are built around the routines of daily life and do not include any interest in wider affairs.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. No monologue/deep thought; talk stays on news, sports, hobbies — no deep critical analysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Limited speech in social settings, since NPCs need a nearby Grey handler to supply their words and fall silent when the handler moves out of range.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. No monologue/deep thought; talk stays on news, sports, hobbies — no deep critical analysis.

questions.hint: No monologue — news, sports, hobbies only; no deep critique.

questions.question: What external outlets construct and maintain an NPC's reality boundaries?

options.label: A

options.rationale: TV, radio, literature, schools = the programming stack that builds NPC reality walls.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct signals from the Moon station, which update each NPC's program every night while it sleeps, with media playing a secondary role in their daily lives.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. TV, radio, literature, schools = the programming stack that builds NPC reality walls.

options.label: C
options.text: Their families and close friends, whose opinions shape what the NPC believes, while the media has little influence on them until they reach adulthood.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. TV, radio, literature, schools = the programming stack that builds NPC reality walls.

options.label: D
options.text: The workplaces they are assigned to, which set the routines and opinions of each NPC through managers trained in the controllers' methods.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. TV, radio, literature, schools = the programming stack that builds NPC reality walls.

questions.hint: TV, radio, literature, educational institutions.

questions.question: How do NPCs perform knowledge they do not actually possess?

options.label: A

options.rationale: True souls retrieve cosmic memory at the Flash; NPCs mimic media, not cosmic archives.

options.label: B
options.text: They never speak and only enforce conformity through complete silence forever.
options.rationale: They speak consensus content and slogans; silence is not their enforcement mode.

options.label: C

options.rationale: Slogan blurts and TV mimicry are named NPC speech patterns.

options.label: D
options.text: They mimic characters from television shows and blurt out mainstream slogans as if they possess actual knowledge.
options.rationale: Mimicry of TV characters and slogan blurts substitute for real knowledge.

options.label: B

options.rationale: They are placed everywhere serving food, driving taxis, teaching, and living as family.

options.label: C
options.text: As permanent 5th density guides who choose new cities freely each morning without scripts.
options.rationale: They cannot reach 5th density; they are scripted static-role constructs in 3rd density sim.

options.label: D
options.text: Like free-roaming Micro Suns with no fixed role and no environmental tether at all.
options.rationale: Like background characters in games such as Grand Theft Auto — tethered to environments and roles.

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: D

options.rationale: Food service, taxis, teachers, family — ubiquitous placement for cohesive restriction.

questions.hint: Everywhere — food, taxis, teachers, close family.

options.label: B
options.text: Children's vessels are grown from the same stem cells as true souls, so they look the same until the age of sixteen.

options.label: C
options.text: The Frequency Fences hide children's NPC programming until they reach school age, when it is switched on for the first time.
options.rationale: Not what the report says. Child NPCs lack fully formed adult String/pride rigidity that makes adult NPCs easier to spot.

options.rationale: Not what the report says. Child NPCs lack fully formed adult String/pride rigidity that makes adult NPCs easier to spot.

questions.question: What ratio vanishes when the holographic alien invasion and 30-second EMF flash hit?

options.label: A
options.text: No one vanishes — only the projection dome brightens with zero demographic change.
options.rationale: 97 of 100 vanish; removal coincides with stripping overlays and the fake projection dome.

options.label: B
options.text: All 100 ascend as NPCs while true souls are relocated under the Vatican permanently.
options.rationale: NPCs vanish; true-soul survivors remain at roughly 3 per 100 in location counts.

options.label: C
options.text: Three of every hundred vanish while ninety-seven remain as permanent herd enforcers.
options.rationale: For every 100 people, 97 instantly vanish, leaving only 3 survivors.

options.label: D
options.text: For every 100 people present in any given location, 97 will instantly vanish, leaving only 3 survivors.
options.rationale: Staged holographic invasion + 30s Flash → 97 vanish, 3 remain per 100.

questions.hint: 97 of 100 vanish — 3 survivors — invasion scare + 30s Flash.

questions.question: How should awakened individuals prepare emotionally for the 97% disappearance?

options.label: A
options.text: By trying to awaken every hardwired NPC so none disappear and attachment never needs release.
options.rationale: Attempting to awaken hardwired matrix beings is futile; release of attachment is required.

options.label: B
options.text: By deepening lifelong grief contracts with every NPC relative as if they were eternal souls.
options.rationale: True souls will not experience sorrow or grief — recognizing NPCs as temporary synthetic constructs.

options.label: C
options.text: Release emotional attachment — friends, colleagues, and close family among the 97% will vanish.
options.rationale: Prepare to release attachment; cosmic memory return prevents grief over synthetic disappearances.

options.label: D
options.text: By refusing all cosmic memory so the Flash produces maximum unresolved mourning by design.
options.rationale: True souls instantly retrieve millions of years of cosmic memory and do not grieve NPCs.

questions.hint: Release attachment — no grief; NPCs recognized as temporary synthetics.

options.label: A

options.rationale: True souls must remain calm and anchored on hidden knowledge while the programmed world panics.

options.label: B
options.text: Completely detach from the 3 Strings; do not let NPC herd mentality dictate reality.
options.rationale: Sever Strings, refuse herd validation games, stop converting NPCs, stay anchored when terror hits.

options.label: C
options.text: Spend the final phase only converting NPCs on television so none need to be erased at the Flash.
options.rationale: Awakening hardwired NPCs is futile; they are designed to derail awakening and punish non-conformity.

options.label: D
options.text: Double down on Religion, Finance, and Perceived Knowledge so the herd accepts you as leader forever.
options.rationale: Allowing NPC herd mentality to dictate reality produces psychological collapse as the old world dissolves.
